The Society was formed by a group of individuals who had jointly undertaken the construction of a residential building comprising twelve (12) dwelling units. The main objects of the Society, as stated in the bye-laws filed at the time of registration, are as follows:

(i) To purchase, take on lease, or otherwise acquire land and buildings for the purpose of providing housing accommodation to its members.

(ii) To construct, alter, repair, and maintain buildings and other structures for the benefit of the members.

(iii) To provide for the common needs of the members, including but not limited to water supply, sanitation, electricity, lifts, parking areas, and security arrangements.

(iv) To borrow money from cooperative banks, scheduled banks, or other financial institutions for the purposes of the Society, with the prior approval of the general body.

(vi) To undertake such other activities as may be conducive to the welfare of the members and the maintenance of the property.

The bye-laws of the Society provide for the following categories of membership:

(a) Ordinary Members: Persons who hold a share or shares in the Society and who are allotted a dwelling unit (flat) in the building. Each ordinary member shall have one vote in the affairs of the Society irrespective of the number of shares held.

(b) Nominal Members: Persons who are admitted as nominal members in accordance with the provisions of the bye-laws. Nominal members shall not have the right to vote and shall not be entitled to any share in the profits or assets of the Society. Nominal membership may be granted to a spouse or dependent of an ordinary member for the purpose of succession.

(c) Associate Members: Any other category of membership as may be approved by the general body from time to time, subject to the provisions of the Act and the Rules.

6. GENERAL BODY MEETINGS

6.1 Annual General Meeting

The Society shall hold an Annual General Meeting (AGM) once in every financial year, within six

(a) confirmation of the minutes of the previous general body meeting;
(b) consideration and adoption of the annual accounts and balance sheet;
(c) appointment of auditors, if not already appointed;
(d) election of the Managing Committee, if due;
(e) transaction of any other business that may be brought before the meeting with the permission of
    the Chairperson.

6.2 Special General Meeting

A Special General Meeting (SGM) may be convened by the Chairperson at any time, and shall be
convened upon a requisition signed by not less than one-fifth of the total number of members,
specifying the business to be transacted. The notice for an SGM shall be issued within fourteen
(14) days of the receipt of such requisition.

6.3 Notice and Quorum

Notice of every general body meeting, along with the agenda, shall be circulated to all members at
least fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting. The quorum for a general body meeting shall
be one-third of the total number of members or fifteen (15) members, whichever is less. If the
quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes of the scheduled time, the meeting shall stand
adjourned to the same day, time, and place in the following week, and the members present at the
adjourned meeting shall constitute the quorum.

7. MANAGING COMMITTEE

7.1 Constitution

The affairs of the Society shall be managed by a Managing Committee consisting of not less than five

The Society was formed by a group of individuals who had jointly undertaken the construction of a residential building comprising twelve (12) dwelling units. The promoters of the Society were desirous of forming a cooperative society under the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, for the purpose of acquiring the land and building, obtaining finance from the cooperative bank, and managing the affairs of the housing complex in a democratic and transparent manner.

The main objects of the Society, as stated in the bye-laws filed at the time of registration, are as follows:

(i) To purchase, take on lease, or otherwise acquire land and buildings for the purpose of providing housing accommodation to its members.

(ii) To construct, alter, repair, and maintain buildings and other structures for the benefit of the members.

(iii) To provide for the common needs of the members, including but not limited to water supply, sanitation, electricity, lifts, parking areas, and security arrangements.

(iv) To borrow money from cooperative banks, scheduled banks, or other financial institutions for the purposes of the Society, with the prior approval of the general body.

(vi) To undertake such other activities as may be conducive to the welfare of the members and the maintenance of the property.

3. MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES

The bye-laws of the Society provide for the following categories of membership:

(a) Ordinary Members: Persons who hold a share or shares in the Society and who are allotted a dwelling unit (flat) in the building. Each ordinary member shall have one vote in the affairs of the Society irrespective of the number of shares held.

(b) Nominal Members: Persons who are admitted as nominal members in accordance with the provisions of the bye-laws. Nominal membership may be granted to a spouse or dependent of an ordinary member for the purpose of succession.

(c) Associate Members: Any other category of membership as may be approved by the general body from time to time, subject to the provisions of the Act and the Rules.

No extension of time shall be granted except under circumstances beyond the contractor's control, as determined by the Managing Committee in its sole discretion.

**4. PAYMENT TERMS**

The contractor shall furnish the necessary PAN/GST details and submit the requisite forms/challans for such deductions.

**5. VARIATIONS AND EXTRA ITEMS**

5.1. Any variation in the scope of work shall be carried out only upon the written approval of the Honorary Secretary. The contractor shall not proceed with any extra work without such prior written approval. Any work executed without such approval shall be at the contractor's own cost and risk.

5.2. The rates for any extra items shall be mutually agreed upon before the commencement of such work. In case of a dispute regarding the rates, the matter shall be referred to the Chairman of the Society, whose decision shall be final and binding on the contractor.

5.3. The contractor shall maintain a site diary and a measurement book in the prescribed format, which shall be made available for inspection by the Society's authorized representative at all reasonable times. All measurements for extra items shall be recorded in the measurement book and signed by both parties.

**6. QUALITY OF MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP**

6.1. All materials used for the work shall be of the best quality and conform to the relevant Indian Standards (IS) specifications. The contractor shall submit the test certificates for all major materials, including the waterproofing compound, primer, and membrane, before their use on site.

6.2. The contractor shall provide samples of the materials to the Honorary Secretary for approval before the commencement of the work. The approved samples shall be kept in the Society office for reference during the work.

6.3. The workmanship shall be of the highest standard, and the contractor shall employ skilled and experienced labor for the work. The contractor shall be solely responsible for the quality of work and shall rectify any defective work at his own cost, within seven days of receiving a written notice from the Society.

6.4. The contractor shall carry out the work in a workmanlike manner and shall take all necessary precautions to avoid damage to the existing structure, plumbing lines, electrical conduits, and other services. Any damage caused due to the contractor's negligence shall be repaired by the contractor at his own cost.

**7. SAFETY AND INSURANCE**

7.1. The contractor shall take all necessary safety precautions during the execution of the work. The contractor shall provide safety equipment, including helmets, safety belts, and safety nets, to all workers engaged in the work. The contractor shall also ensure that the workers are not exposed to hazardous conditions.

7.2. The contractor shall be responsible for the safety of all persons and property at the site and shall comply with all applicable safety regulations and bye-laws. The contractor shall also keep the site clean and tidy and shall remove all debris and waste material at regular intervals.

7.3. The contractor shall, at his own cost, take out and maintain the following insurance policies for the duration of the work:
- **Workmen's Compensation Policy** covering all workers engaged in the work, in accordance with the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923.
- **Public Liability Insurance Policy** for a sum of not less than Rs. 10,00,000 (Rupees Ten Lakh only) to cover any third-party claims for bodily injury or property damage arising out of the work.
- **Contractor's All Risk Policy** covering the work in progress, including materials and equipment, for the full contract value.
